claims: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission.
Artemis II will fly around the moon.
Artemis II marks the first human spaceflight to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
The rocket and spacecraft are scheduled to roll to the launch pad on March 19, 2026.
Artemis II mission duration is approximately 10 days.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft, according to NASA.
Artemis II goal is testing systems for deep space, according to NASA.
Reid Wiseman is the Commander of the Artemis II crew, according to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
Victor Glover is the Pilot of the Artemis II crew, according to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
Christina Koch is a Mission Specialist on Artemis II, according to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
Jeremy Hansen is a Mission Specialist on Artemis II, according to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
Artemis II mission was previously delayed from earlier in 2026 due to technical issues, including heat shield repairs and cold weather testing, as reported by Spaceflight Now and Space.
